# The formation generated by a finite group can have infinitely many subformations

There is
a finite group $G$ such that infinitely many formations are contained in the formation generated
by $G$. That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 16.31 is negative, even for finite $G$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 16.31 (V. A. Vedernikov); resolution: V. P. Burichenko, J. Algebra 372 (2012), 428-458, Kourovka Archive, Problem 16.31 (No, not always, even for G finite).
